To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the warpage of large dies can be reduced by tuning the dielectric layers stress, and that the model is very accurate to predict the bow.

1) the bow can be reduced to less than 50 m using a stress tuning of the interposer dielectric layers, 2) the bow of the large die is not affected by the thermal cycles, 3) a bow less than or equal to 50 m can be obtained for a 650 m2 interposer, 4) the bow range is reduced from 100 to 50 m by using a symmetrical interposer design

the warpage of the Si interposer is successfully managed using the three levers mentioned above, and that the bow range over the thermal cycle is less than 50 micrometers for the 300 mm die, and less than 30 micrometers for both the 200 mm die and the 650 mm interposer
In summary, our research is concerned with
the warpage control of the interposer, which is the key issue to achieve a high yield assembly.
the warpage of dissymmetrical structures and the bow management of large dies.
the development of a new generation of computing packages for high reliability applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the warpage of the Si interposer is successfully managed and the bow of the large die is reduced by more than a factor 2.
this study demonstrates the feasibility of a large die stacking on a ceramic substrate with a bow less than the 3 mm limit for a mass reflow process.
a bow less than the 50 mm target is obtained with the proposed methodology and process flow.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bow of the 300 mm die is reduced to 12 mm, the bow of the interposer is reduced to 50 mm and the bow of the whole package is reduced to 60 mm.

the interposer bow reduction from 230 to 12 mm is obtained thanks to the optimization of three parameters: the thickness of the interposer, the stress of the passivation layer, and the symmetry of both faces.
the interposer warpage can be managed with the right design and processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a very accurate bow model is needed for a good yield of the assembly process.
a 50 mm bow is achievable for a large die interposer on a 650 x 650 mm2 substrate with a 450 ball pitch, which opens the door to 3D assembly of large dies.
the bow can be reduced to 50 mm with a 725 mm thick interposer and that a 200 mm thick Si die can be assembled on a 725 mm interposer without warpage issue.
